jsx_dom_conclusion: MIT LICENSE in @gera2ld/jsx-dom 2.2.2 tarball matches byte-for-byte tag v2.2.2 commit 9f9660e94280e642ee6ba8e644a3f2cd8903f7e1/LICENSE; both package.json sources and bundle banners say ISC. For this distribution retain the explicit MIT grant and ISC declarations, without claiming upstream dual licensing or legal resolution. Upstream correction remains outstanding.

gaps.details: Recovered the literal ISC LICENSE from upstream commit be0bcd8a4e917a0a5895e95b523fbbed05a64871 (2015-10-14). Its index.js is byte-identical to the complete executable member of boolbase 1.0.0 npm tarball (Git blob 8799fd95dbe31a85c48b956eb19f3625da9f8fb1). The commit still declares version 1.0.0 and ISC; package.json differs in scripts and is not claimed byte-identical. This is a later upstream license addition, not a file in the original npm tarball or proof of Markmap bundle inclusion. Both original metadata and recovered grant are retained.

KaTeX 0.16.21 and 0.16.47 dist/katex.mjs explicitly attribute hyphenate and escape adaptations to Facebook React under Apache 2. The literal comment is retained with byte ranges for both versions. Their npm packages contain only the top-level MIT LICENSE. The exact adapted React revision, corresponding copyright and complete applicable notices have not been established; the comment alone does not close that chain.

All 60 versioned package locators in Mermaid 11.17.2 sourcemap have primary license texts. Nested prebundles such as roughjs, Cytoscape, KaTeX and d3-delaunay can inline further origins not exposed as separate sourcemap packages. No complete recursive inventory or legal clearance is asserted. roughjs locator retains the upstream patch hash; 664 source contents match exact npm members, 11 marked TypeScript members are absent from its published tarball.

D3 7.8.5 dependency versions are taken from its v7.8.5 yarn.lock, not semver ranges. Several package source fragments match its unminified dist member. No full source-to-minified rebuild or release attestation proves every locked package was embedded.

Markmap 0.17.2 published package.json gitHead bbeec32d0efeea4e36755b1909a5993187264487 identifies an upstream pnpm lockfile. Collected candidate dependency licenses are a conservative superset; the tarballs lack sourcemaps and a full rebuild has not established exact inclusion of every candidate. d3-flextree 2.1.2 is explicit; its d3-hierarchy 1.1.9 comes from the release lock. Browser view uses global d3; lib uses global katex.

MIT LICENSE in @gera2ld/jsx-dom 2.2.2 tarball matches byte-for-byte tag v2.2.2 commit 9f9660e94280e642ee6ba8e644a3f2cd8903f7e1/LICENSE; both package.json sources and bundle banners say ISC. For this distribution retain the explicit MIT grant and ISC declarations, without claiming upstream dual licensing or legal resolution. Upstream correction remains outstanding.

Cytoscape 3.34.0 exact dist member matches the Mermaid source content. Retained its MIT text and literal Thenable/Ralf Engelschall, jQuery events, Gaetan Renaudeau Bezier, Koen Bok Framer and Gerardo Huck CoSE attributions with byte ranges. The adapted jQuery/Bezier/Framer excerpts do not identify immutable upstream revisions; no invented package version or fabricated copyright/license pairing closes that chain.

Mermaid 11.17.2 embeds DOMPurify 3.4.12, covered by GHSA-55q2-fjhq-7xh7 (patched 3.4.13). The same dependency was observed in Mermaid 12.0.0; no custom bundle substitution is made. Advisory requires IN_PLACE plus an element-removal hook; applicability/exploitability in AI Docs has not been established.

Markmap 0.17.2 embeds markdown-it code and its release gitHead locks 14.1.0, covered by GHSA-6v5v-wf23-fmfq, GHSA-253c-mchw-3w2r and GHSA-r7fv-28h4-cvq7. Markmap 0.18.12 latest release gitHead also locks 14.1.0, so an unrelated upgrade would not close this. No custom patch to published bundles. Direct markdown-it vendor is 14.3.2; that does not replace Markmap internal parser.
